notes:
Summary: Novaforge is evaluating Redwood Dedicated to replace part of their in-house inference fleet for the personalization stack. Primary focus: throughput guarantees and predictable reserved capacity for heavy reranking at peak shopping times.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-01-15: Intro call (Jordan + Ruth) — quick product fit, Novaforge confirms interest in Dedicated pool and VPC.
- 2026-02-18: POC kickoff (fireflies ff_2026-02-18_novaforge_poc_kickoff) — validated basic latency and correctness on small test queries.
- 2026-02-25: Architecture deep-dive with infra (Ruth, infra engs) — discussed KV cache, batching, and model variants.
- 2026-03-03: Throughput modeling workshop — ran scenarios for Black Friday-like peaks; draft GPU counts produced.
- 2026-03-09: Pricing & SLA negotiation call (Jordan, Amina, Novaforge CTO Lara Kim) — agreed on target metrics to put in SOW.

Use-case details and targets:
- Workload: Reranking + semantic search supporting 2M daily sessions; re-rank requests average 12 candidates; typical prompt length 250 tokens; heavy bursts during promos.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 180ms for rerank (single-request end-to-end token generation), p99 < 400ms preferred for core routes.
- Throughput targets: guaranteed sustained baseline of 15000 tokens/sec across reserved pool for rerank+search, ability to handle spikes to ~60k tokens/sec for up to 10 minutes (burst policy) without failed requests.
- Concurrency: plan for 120 concurrent active sessions routed to Dedicated pool; soft concurrency cap of 200 with degraded latency allowed during bursts.
- Reserved GPUs: preliminary estimate = 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (or equivalent vram profiles) with headroom for 20% growth; want explicit mapping in SOW for min tokens/sec per GPU and acceptable throttling behavior.
- Fallbacks: must support automatic fallback to hosted-compatible model variant in other region with durable queuing rather than request rejection.

SLA / commercial asks from Novaforge:
- Minimum committed tokens/sec and guaranteed concurrency floor in contract.
- Clear burst policy: duration, throttling vs. queueing, and pricing for burst consumption beyond commit.
- Credits/backstop for missed SLOs tied to business impact windows (e.g., peak sale hours).
- Runbook access and incident contact (24x7 on-call) for production incidents.

Open items & negotiation points:
- How Redwood measures tokens/sec (client-side vs. server-side accounting) — Novaforge wants server-side accounting and transparent logs per-route.
- Definition of 'burst' window and how many bursts per month allowed without penalty.
- Concurrency accounting: whether idle sessions count toward concurrency caps (Novaforge requests per-request concurrency accounting).
- Mapping of model variants to token throughput guarantees — need appendix listing supported quantized variants and expected per-GPU throughput.

Quotes / customer color:
- Lara Kim (CTO): "We need guarantees for peak promo hours — last year tail latency cost us $1.2M in lost conversions. If we can't rely on throughput, we won't move core rerank to Redwood."
- Head of Infra (email): "If you can commit tokens/sec per GPU we can size remaining infra and accelerate migration."

Technical notes for SE follow-up:
- Provide per-model perf matrix (tokens/sec per GPU at 250-token avg and at 1024-token cases).
- Include recommended continuous-batching knobs and cache TTL for rerank flows.
- Outline autoscale/burst policy: warm standby capacity, fast spin-up time, and expected cold-start token impact.
- Provide sample SLO language for min tokens/sec, concurrency caps, and credit calculations for violations.

Next steps (short):
- Draft SOW with explicit min tokens/sec, concurrency model, and burst pricing (Ruth) — due 2026-03-17.
- Legal to review SLA and credit terms (Amina) — target 2026-03-24.
- Novaforge to confirm EU data residency for 30% of traffic (Lara) — blocker for go-live.

Attachments & refs: pricing deck (drive:/deals/novaforge/Novaforge_Redwood_SOW_v1.pdf), security questionnaire (drive:/security/novaforge/security-questionnaire.xlsx), early perf report (attached in thread-CA12345-novaforge-sla).

CRM shorthand / call notes:
- POC looks good for functional quality; perf margin close to target but depends on quantized variant selection.
- Novaforge price-sensitive on burst rates; wants firm burst caps to avoid surprise costs.
- High likelihood to close if SOW includes tokens/sec guarantee + credits for SLO misses.
